claims.claim: **In infants and young children the symptoms are frequently non-specific**: fever · poor feeding · vomiting · lethargy · irritability · jaundice · faltering growth. Older children present more typically: dysuria, frequency, new daytime accidents, haematuria, abdominal or loin pain.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Urinary tract infection' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Urinary_tract_infection/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Consider UTI in any child whose fever without a focus persists beyond 48 hours.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Urinary tract infection' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Urinary_tract_infection/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Cystitis** suggests frequency, urgency, dysuria and lower abdominal discomfort; **pyelonephritis** suggests fever, rigors, malaise, vomiting and loin tenderness. The distinction is hard in younger children.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Urinary tract infection' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Urinary_tract_infection/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Atypical UTI** = seriously ill · septicaemia · no response to antibiotics within 48 hours · a non-*E. coli* organism · poor urine flow · raised creatinine · abdominal or bladder mass.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Urinary tract infection' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Urinary_tract_infection/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Urine is not needed** when the fever has another clear focus and the child is not systemically unwell.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Urinary tract infection' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Urinary_tract_infection/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Collect the sample before antibiotics** — except when a seriously unwell child needs IV therapy straight away.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Urinary tract infection' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Urinary_tract_infection/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Suprapubic aspirate is the gold standard up to 6 months.** Midstream urine for toilet-trained children; clean catch for pre-continent children who are not seriously unwell.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Urinary tract infection' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Urinary_tract_infection/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Bag urine is not recommended for culture** — high false-positive rates.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Urinary tract infection' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Urinary_tract_infection/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Clean the perineum with saline-soaked gauze for 10 seconds; do not use antiseptic.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Urinary tract infection' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Urinary_tract_infection/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Dipstick screens; culture with pyuria confirms.** Dipstick is less reliable in neonates and young infants, mainly through false negatives.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Urinary tract infection' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Urinary_tract_infection/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Send for culture if:** under 3 months · leukocyte esterase or nitrite positive · suspected upper UTI · recurrent UTI · not responding in 24–48 hours · clinical UTI despite an unremarkable dipstick.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Urinary tract infection' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Urinary_tract_infection/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Absent nitrites do not exclude UTI**; blood and protein are not reliable markers.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Urinary tract infection' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Urinary_tract_infection/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Febrile, unwell infants under 4 weeks:** FBE, blood culture and LP, and admit for IV antibiotics.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Urinary tract infection' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Urinary_tract_infection/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Admit any seriously unwell child and every infant under 3 months for initial IV antibiotics.** For other children with uncomplicated UTI, oral treatment is usually appropriate.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Urinary tract infection' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Urinary_tract_infection/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Duration: 3–5 days for cystitis; 7–10 days for pyelonephritis.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Urinary tract infection' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Urinary_tract_infection/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Cystitis:** oral cefalexin three times daily, 20 mg/kg (up to 750 mg).
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Urinary tract infection' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Urinary_tract_infection/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Pyelonephritis, oral:** cefalexin — under 12 months, 25 mg/kg (up to 1 g) four times daily; from 12 months, 45 mg/kg (up to 1.5 g) three times daily.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Urinary tract infection' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Urinary_tract_infection/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Do not delay antibiotics in a seriously unwell child** to obtain urine. **Empiric IV: gentamicin**; check levels and renal function if continuing beyond 48 hours, and consider a 3rd-generation cephalosporin if IV therapy will be prolonged.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Urinary tract infection' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Urinary_tract_infection/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Switch to oral when clinically improved or tolerating oral.** Local susceptibility patterns and prior microbiology should guide the empiric choice.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Urinary tract infection' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Urinary_tract_infection/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Renal tract ultrasound:** all children with atypical UTI, and infants under 6 months with recurrent UTI or without antenatal monitoring. **Most children do not need an ultrasound for a first UTI.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Urinary tract infection' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Urinary_tract_infection/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Routine antibiotic prophylaxis is not generally recommended.** Arrange specialist follow-up for recurrent UTI or known renal anomalies.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Urinary tract infection' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Urinary_tract_infection/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Consider an STI screen in sexually active young people.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Urinary tract infection' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Urinary_tract_infection/, retrieved 2026-09-23
